events.title: Fire Follows You Home
events.body: A storm left a burning bush, and one of you has carried a brand back to the cave. The smoke stings, the elders call it bad luck, and the night animals disagree with everything. Keeping fire means tending it every single night, forever. Letting it go means warmth stays a rumor.

choices.label: Feed it all night
choices.quote: Warmth is a job with no weekends.

events.title: The Best Hunter Gives Meat Away
events.body: Your best hunter keeps handing out haunches to people who brought nothing. Nobody is starving and everybody is talking. Status, it turns out, is something you get by losing calories on purpose. The other bands are starting to notice whose cave has the loudest gratitude.

choices.label: Make it official: feasts on schedule

events.title: First Tool, Second Opinions
events.body: Somebody chipped a stone into an edge that actually works. The invention is spreading faster than anyone can claim credit for it, which is exactly the problem some of you would like to file a complaint about.

choices.label: Credit the inventor publicly
choices.quote: Naming things is the first trademark.

choices.label: Keep it secret within your family

events.title: Someone Dies (It's Not the End of You)
events.body: A hunting accident, thoroughly preventable, involving a bison and a decision. The band must decide what your name means now that one mouth carrying it has stopped. The lineage continues through someone smaller, younger, and deeply unqualified.

choices.label: Give the heir your unfinished tool
Declare the death bad luck and move camp

events.title: The River Has Two Banks
events.body: Salmon on one side, berries on the other, winter agreeing to arrive soon. Moving the whole band costs calories you may not have. Staying means betting the season on one bank's opinion.

choices.label: Build a platform over the shallows

events.title: The Stranger at the Fire
events.body: A limping outsider from a burned-out band asks to sit down. Letting them in costs food and might bring enemies. Turning them away costs something nobody can itemize until later.

choices.label: Take them in, make them earn it

events.title: Night Count
events.body: Something large has been visiting the camp's edge at night, testing who's awake. The band looks to whoever holds the fire-tending schedule, which is quietly becoming the most powerful job in the cave.

choices.label: Chase it with torches
choices.quote: We are now friends with fire.

events.title: Ochre Handprints
events.body: Someone presses a painted hand on the cave wall and refuses to explain why. Others want hands next to it. There is a fight about placement, which is the first art controversy and will not be the last.

choices.label: Claim the best wall for the lineage
Open the wall to everyone
choices.quote: The first public forum was dirt.

choices.label: Paint over it with your own hand

events.title: The Long Cold
events.body: A winter that overstays by design. Stores say no. The body count says maybe. Elders propose walking south; the sick propose staying; the very young propose eating the seed stores, which is a proposal in the worst sense.

choices.label: Eat the seed stores
choices.quote: Borrowed from next year, at loan-shark rates.

events.title: Rival Band, Same Cave
events.body: Another lineage wants your shelter, and both of you have discovered that diplomacy is cheaper than the alternative, though nobody has written down either price yet.

choices.label: Fight for it
choices.quote: The rent is paid in teeth.

choices.label: Trade instead: tools for their berry grounds
choices.quote: The first deal had no lawyers. Suspicious.

events.title: Dreaming About Tomorrow
events.body: The shaman insists the future visited her in a dream and said your lineage ends badly unless you stop doing something specific she refuses to specify until after payment. Half the cave is already nervous.

choices.label: Pay the shaman
choices.quote: Consulting fees exist in every economy.

events.title: The Child Who Asks Why
events.body: A child keeps asking why the fire is hot, why the stars don't fall, and why the answer is always 'because.' It is exhausting. It is also, somehow, the beginning of everything. The band must decide whether questions are a resource or a nuisance.

choices.label: Tell the child to ask the shaman
Make the child fire-tender
choices.quote: Prometheus got his start on night shifts.

events.title: First Granary, Two Policies
events.body: The surplus needs a building, and the building needs a policy. Hoard it and you're rich until the neighbors develop opinions about your walls. Feast everyone and you're beloved until winter audits the calendar.

choices.label: Grain temple: store it, lend it
choices.quote: Granaries were banks before banks had the decency to be invisible.

events.title: The Irrigation Question
events.body: Water is a mile away and the river disagrees with your field layout. A ditch feeds everyone for years and enslaves everyone for seasons. Somebody has to organize the digging, and that somebody acquires a title by the end of it.

choices.label: Dig the communal ditch
choices.quote: Civilization is a trench filled with water and complaints.

choices.label: Stay near the river, accept floods

events.title: Debt Is Invented
events.body: A farmer borrows seed against next harvest and discovers he cannot repay it, and that his daughter is legally considered collateral. The village looks to the granary-keeper — you — to decide whether debts have ceilings.

choices.label: Enforce the debt
choices.quote: Contracts are contracts. Say it gently.

choices.label: Cancel it publicly
choices.quote: Debt jubilee: popular then, expensive now.

choices.label: Cap future interest
choices.quote: Regulation: invented immediately before it was hated.

events.title: The Calendar Dispute
events.body: Planting day is a matter of opinion, and the two opinions are three weeks apart and both religious. Whoever arbitrates becomes, accidentally, the state.

choices.label: Back the astronomers
choices.quote: Science wins; half the valley sulks.

events.title: Locusts Read the Ledger
events.body: Locusts arrive with the confidence of auditors. The stores will last two months if shared, four if rationed, zero if panic takes the gates off the granary first.

choices.label: Lock it, guard it
choices.quote: Walls work until they're the map.

choices.label: Sell to neighbors at famine prices
choices.quote: Every era invents this job. Nobody's proud of it.

events.title: Walls Around the Yard
events.body: Raiders took a sack from the outer field. The village proposes a wall. A wall protects the grain and defines who's inside it, which is a question with a sharper edge than flint.

choices.label: Wall the granary only
choices.quote: Protect the asset, expose the rest.

events.title: The Ox Breakthrough
events.body: Somebody harnesses an ox to a drag-stick and doubles the planted acreage. The landless laborers notice that their value just dropped, and they notice it loudly, at your gate, at dawn.

choices.label: Tax the plough to feed the displaced
choices.quote: Compromise: everyone slightly unhappy, nobody starving.

choices.label: Ban the plough
choices.quote: The Luddite motion, six thousand years early.

events.title: Treaty of the Water Rights
events.body: Upstream villages control the river and would like something for the view. They propose a treaty carved in stone. Stone is durable; so are grievances.

events.title: The First Census
events.body: Counting people is boring until you realize the list decides who eats first. Your scribe now holds more quiet power than the harvest festival suggests.

choices.label: Let the powerful undercount themselves
choices.quote: Corruption: the grease that runs the throne.

events.title: Priest-King Wants a Temple
events.body: The high priest proposes a temple funded by a grain tithe, promising divine yield forecasts accurate to within one season. The forecast is wrong every time. The temple, however, compounds.

choices.label: Redirect the tithe to the ditch
choices.quote: Infrastructure vs. incense. Incense lobbies harder.

events.title: Seed Selection, Season Forty
events.body: Decades of saving the hardiest seed are quietly rewriting the grass. The new strain yields double and tastes like wet cardboard, and it roots deeper when raiders trample the top.

choices.label: Commit fully to the new strain
choices.quote: Genetic monoculture: the empire's coming food allergy.

choices.label: Keep old strains as backup
choices.quote: A seed vault is a letter to the future.

events.title: The Elder Who Remembers Too Much
events.body: The oldest member of the village remembers three famines, two treaties, and precisely who broke each one. Writing is arriving, and there is a debate about which version of events gets carved. The elder has opinions about the editing process.

choices.label: Carve both, side by side
choices.quote: Footnotes cause wars eventually. Worth it.

events.title: The Tin Route Delegation
events.body: The tin road — bronze's supply chain — runs through four kingdoms and a strait controlled by people with toll booths. Negotiating it requires sending somebody. A slave trader offers services cheaply and results expensively. Your own son would be trustworthy, and is also collateral.

choices.label: Send the trader
choices.quote: Cheap envoy, costly fine print. [Chronicle flag: lineage clause — resurfaces Era 11.]

choices.label: Send your son
choices.quote: Trust is a hedge with a face.

events.title: Debased Coin, Rising Expectations
events.body: Treasury math says the legions can be paid in coin with less silver in it. The legions have scales. Loyalty and currency integrity are on a collision course and both report to you.

choices.label: Raise taxes to keep the silver
Cut legion size
choices.quote: Cheaper army, longer frontier, shorter life.

events.title: Write the Law Down
events.body: Judges have been improvising verdicts according to whichever family visits them first. A reformer proposes carving the laws in public. Literacy being what it is, 'public' means 'where the powerful must squint at it collectively.'

choices.label: Publish the code
choices.quote: Rule of law: predictability, priced per column.

events.title: Roads Are Arguments
events.body: The treasury proposes paving the trade road. Paving wins the argument with mud permanently; maintenance loses the argument with entropy annually, forever.

choices.label: Pave the main road
choices.quote: Every mile paved recruits a mile of decay.

choices.label: Privilege a toll-concession
choices.quote: Roads work; barons emerge. Net unclear.

events.title: Palace Accounts
events.body: The palace books show three treasuries, none reconciling, all staffed by relatives. An auditor volunteer appears — genuinely competent, structurally unwelcome.

events.title: The Philosopher's Invoice
events.body: A school of philosophers petitions for state funding, offering 'truth' as the deliverable. Their tuition bill arrives quarterly regardless of truth delivery rate.

events.title: Plague on the Trade Road
events.body: Illness travels the routes faster than tin. Quarantine the roads and trade strangles; keep them open and the census files itself.

choices.label: Keep trade open
choices.quote: The market's immune system is cruel.

events.title: Overextension Notice
events.body: Three frontier garrisons request pay, grain, and a reason to exist. The core provinces request lower taxes. Geography requests that you stop requesting things of it.

choices.label: Withdraw from the far province
choices.quote: Realism reads as betrayal from outside the map.

choices.label: Subcontract borders to client kings
choices.quote: Outsourcing sovereignty: excellent margins, terrible reviews later.

events.title: The Library Copy Problem
events.body: The royal library's scrolls are aging. Scribes can recopy ten percent this year: agricultural manuals, naval charts, or the epic poems that legitimize the dynasty.

choices.label: Copy the technical texts
choices.quote: Utility over glory; nobody sings about crop rotation.

choices.label: Copy a bit of everything
choices.quote: A compromise archive; mediocre at all things.

events.title: Corporations Begin Badly
events.body: Merchant houses petition the crown for legal personhood: the right to own, sue, and outlive their founders. Clever. Possibly catastrophic. Definitely profitable.

choices.label: Grant charters
choices.quote: Immortality, incorporated. Royalty pioneered it; nobody else could afford it.

choices.label: Deny; personal liability only
choices.quote: Owners answer for owners. Radically unfashionable.

events.title: The General With Popular Support
events.body: A victorious general returns loved by the legions and the mob, in that order. History has a word for men like him and the word is not 'retired.'

choices.label: Co-opt: marry him into the lineage
choices.quote: Family is the oldest HR department.

choices.label: Retire him. Firmly
choices.quote: The Republic lasts another generation. The rumors do too.

events.title: Coin Reforms, Third Attempt
events.body: Neighboring powers mint your currency as counterfeit, badly enough to undercut it, well enough to fool markets. Recoinage costs a fortune; tolerance costs the standard.

choices.label: Free-market shrug
choices.quote: Let quality speak. Quality is slow and currently losing.

events.title: The Scriptorium Budget
events.body: Parchment is scarce, monks are patient, and the shelf holds choices: a farming manual, a holy text, or a Roman engineering codex. Each copy preserves a world; there is vellum for one path this year. [Callback flag: whichever is copied resurfaces in Era 9 as the digitized archive.]

choices.label: Copy the farming manual
choices.quote: Bread over doctrine. The harvest votes.

choices.label: Copy the holy text
choices.quote: Salvation ships today; agronomy deprecates quietly.

events.title: Knowledge Decay, Routine
events.body: Three shelves have rotted past reading and the abbot confesses nobody recopied them since before his vows. Forgetting is not an event here; it's weather.

choices.label: Prioritize salvage copies
choices.quote: Manuscripts eat monks slower than wolves do.

choices.label: Let it rot; record the titles
choices.quote: A catalog of losses is still a catalog.

events.title: The Hill Chief's Protection Offer
events.body: A local warlord offers sword-protection for the monastery's grain. His definition of protection overlaps significantly with his appetite, and his literacy is aspirational.

events.title: The Relic Economy
events.body: A bone arrives claiming sainthood. Believers arrive claiming cures. The relic's provenance is fictional and the pilgrim revenue is real.

choices.label: Authenticate the relic
choices.quote: Faith-based auditing finds what faith requires.

choices.label: Expose the fraud
choices.quote: Truth: a downgrade to cash flow.

choices.label: Sell authentication certificates
choices.quote: Indulgences debut early. The audit comes due; it always does.

events.title: The Viking Winter
events.body: Longships appear upriver with the precision of a delivery service. The monastery holds gold cups, jeweled covers, and zero swords.

choices.label: Pay the danegeld
choices.quote: Tribute: recurring billing with worse service.

choices.label: Hide the books, lose the gold
choices.quote: They take the metal; we keep the meaning.

events.title: The Heresy File
events.body: A monk's marginalia contradicts accepted doctrine and, inconveniently, is correct. The bishop requests the notes. The abbot requests advice. The monk requests patience.

choices.label: Archive the notes privately
choices.quote: The forbidden shelf is always the interesting shelf.

choices.label: Litigate it slowly
choices.quote: Councils: centuries of procedure, inches of outcome.

events.title: The Plague Parish
events.body: Illness walks the valley. The parish faces the same arithmetic as every collapse: flee and live with it, stay and possibly die with honor, or quarantine the village and decide who counts as family.

choices.label: Flee with the library
choices.quote: The books survived beautifully decorated funerals.

events.title: The Lost Roman Road
events.body: Surveyors find a paved road still intact under three centuries of bramble. Clearing it restores a trade link; the local lord fears it also restores invaders' GPS.

choices.label: Clear the road
choices.quote: Gridlock returns; so does gridlock's clientele.

choices.label: Keep it secret, use it yourselves
Leave it buried
choices.quote: The forest was a better customs agent than anyone admits.

events.title: Christening the Old Gods
events.body: The countryside still leaves offerings at the spring. Missionary strategy demands a choice: outlaw the spring, or christen it and let the old gods retire under new management, same duties, revised paperwork.

choices.label: Outlaw the old rites
choices.quote: Persecution: expensive enforcement of unverifiable claims.

choices.label: Ignore both; collect taxes either way

events.title: The Chronicle Continues
events.body: The annals break off mid-sentence during the last chaos. Restarting the Chronicle means choosing where to begin: glorify the gap, document it honestly, or imply the missing century was a collective hallucination.

choices.label: Begin honestly: 'here we lost the thread.'
Date everything from the restart
choices.quote: Year One energy; calendar confusion forever.

events.title: The Wandering Scholar
events.body: A scholar arrives with a chest of manuscripts from the fallen east — Aristotle-shaped boxes, medical treatises, star tables — and wants lodging, protection, and tenure.

choices.label: Shelter him and copy his chest
choices.quote: Ideas crossed the Dark Ages hiding in trunks.

choices.label: Turn him in as a sorcerer
choices.quote: The bonfire was efficient. Terribly efficient.

events.title: Harvest of Ashes
events.body: Volcanic haze dims the sun; the harvest fails across the continent. Every granary in Christendom is empty by Advent, and your preserved knowledge is worth nothing because nobody can eat a codex. Yet.

choices.label: Break the seals; distribute church stores
choices.quote: The reliquary fed fourteen families. Reportedly.

choices.label: Trade relics for grain from unburnt regions
choices.quote: Sacred objects become commodities exactly once per collapse.

events.title: The Press Investment
events.body: A goldsmith's screw press is for sale: it sets type faster than any scribe and makes errors at industrial scale for the first time in history. Financing it means betting the ledger on cheap pages.

choices.label: Fund the press
choices.quote: Movable type: the original disruptive vertical.

choices.label: Own the paper mill upstream
choices.quote: He who owns the substrate owns the argument.

events.title: Plague Year, Two Doors
events.body: The sickness is in the city. Fleeing preserves the lineage and loses clients, commissions, and the archive's lease. Quarantining buys legitimacy at population's expense.

choices.label: Quarantine the district
choices.quote: Rings around neighborhoods: public health, iron band.

choices.label: Keep the press running outside town
choices.quote: The epidemic slowed; the edition didn't.

events.title: The Patron's Dilemma
events.body: A banking family offers a fortune for a dedication: your name on their patronage, their accounting under your protection. Their money is laundered through art so thick you could frame it twice.

choices.label: Decline on principle
choices.quote: Poverty has excellent reviews and terrible cash flow.

choices.label: Counter: fund a public library in their name

events.title: The Anatomist's Petition
events.body: A physician requests permission to study actual cadavers rather than authoritative texts, which are wrong authoritatively. The guild and the diocese have pre-registered objections jointly.

events.title: Index of Forbidden Pamphlets
events.body: A heretical pamphlet is outperforming your official publications three to one. The bishop wants a ban; the market wants volume; both use the word 'souls.'

choices.label: Print it yourself, annotated
choices.quote: If you can't censor it, edit it.

choices.label: Let the marketplace of ideas brawl

events.title: The Double-Entry Revelation
events.body: A monk-accountant publishes a method where every debit has a credit. Ledger fraud drops forty percent overnight and rises again within a generation, now more sophisticated.

events.title: The Navigator's Speculative Voyage
events.body: A captain proposes a westward route to spice markets, requesting ships and offering wonder. Expected returns are either ruinous or historic, and he cannot honestly distinguish which.

choices.label: Refuse; watch competitors fund it
choices.quote: Discovery happened anyway. Not to us.

choices.label: Fund two rival captains
choices.quote: Hedged exploration: history's first dual listing.

events.title: The Forgery Workshop
events.body: An artist's workshop produces antique-looking antiquities that collectors adore and scholars increasingly authenticate. Revenue is strong; provenance is a fiction with brushstrokes.

choices.label: Rebrand: 'in the antique manner.'
choices.quote: Truth in labeling; fraud in mood.

choices.label: Buy the best pieces for the public collection

events.title: The Star Table Heresy
events.body: The new astronomy's tables predict eclipses better than the old ones and place Earth somewhere embarrassing. Use the heretical tables and admit measurement beats scripture; use the approved ones and keep calendars wrong with confidence.

choices.label: Use the new tables
choices.quote: The data shipped; the cosmology lagged.

choices.label: Commission a compromise cosmology
choices.quote: Epicycles: elegant patches on a wrong foundation.

choices.label: Silently adopt, publicly deny
choices.quote: Hypocrisy: the interoperability layer of eras.

events.title: The Printing Strike
events.body: Type-setters strike over piece-rates because the press doubled output and halved rates per page, a development they characterize as 'the machine stealing bread.' Their argument will be recycled, with better suits, forever.

choices.label: Profit-share on volume
choices.quote: Align incentives before the presses align against you.

events.title: The Siege of the Library
events.body: Army or fire — the distinction stops mattering — approaches the region's greatest collection. Transport capacity saves a fraction. Choosing which fraction is choosing which future gets read.

choices.label: Save the technical corpus
choices.quote: Engines of the next era, mule-back.

choices.label: Save the literary canon
choices.quote: The soul of the age, catalogued.

choices.label: Copy the fastest-moving texts first; abandon the rest

events.title: The Copied Error Goes Viral
events.body: A typo in an early printed medical text — one dosage symbol transposed — is now in four hundred copies and climbing, because presses replicate mistakes with a fidelity scribes never achieved. Corrections travel slower than errors.

choices.label: Buy and burn the bad edition
choices.quote: Censorship of our own product. Efficient.

events.title: The Luddite Visit
events.body: A mob stands before your automated frames with hammers and a petition, historically in that order of effectiveness. Their math is honest: machines took piecework. Your math is honest too: competitors automate or die.

choices.label: Automate harder
choices.quote: Efficiency won the meeting; the street hasn't adjourned.

choices.label: Private guards on the roof
choices.quote: The Peterloo option. History files it under 'P.'

events.title: The Child Labor Vote
events.body: Parliament puts reform on the floor: minimum ages, maximum hours. Your mills run on small hands and larger profits. The factories will relocate if regulated; the children will remain if the factories do.

choices.label: Comply nominally; 'family apprenticeships.'
choices.quote: Loopholes are compliance with extra steps.

events.title: Railway Mania
events.body: Every town wants a line, every speculator wants a station, and share prices have detached from anything as vulgar as terrain. Building anyway adds network value; pulling out preserves capital and reputation for the crash.

events.title: The Smog Audit
events.body: A physician publishes mortality statistics linking your works and air to lung deaths, complete with names. The works employ half the county; the county is dying measurably.

choices.label: Dispute the statistics
choices.quote: Doubt is a product; this one's defective.

events.title: The Engine Patent Trap
events.body: Your engineer's high-efficiency valve design is blocked by a patent thicket held by a competitor who manufactures nothing, litigates everything, and wears the word 'innovation' as a costume.

choices.label: Pay the licensing toll
choices.quote: Patent trolls predate the internet by 170 years.

choices.label: Design around it
choices.quote: Reverse engineering: free speech with blueprints.

events.title: The Great Exhibition Temptation
events.body: The world's fair invites your machinery to a glass palace beside the world's machinery. Displays cost fortunes; impressions convert to export orders; espionage comes with the visitor tickets.

choices.label: Skip the fair; poach exhibited engineers
choices.quote: Exhibits walk away carrying your R&D.

events.title: The Union Recognition Question
events.body: The craft unions propose collective bargaining: orderly strikes, written procedures, no hammers. An alternative to mob math exists, and management finds it almost as frightening as mobs.

events.title: The Boiler Explosion
events.body: A works boiler fails during shift change. Casualties, inquiries, and the discovery that safety inspections were 'deferred for throughput.' The inspector general enjoys paperwork the way boilers enjoy pressure.

events.title: Coal Futures, Sunlight Derivatives
events.body: The exchange lists coal futures and suddenly stockpiled Carboniferous sunshine trades at a premium on winter forecasts. Hedging protects margins; speculation protects egos.

choices.label: Hedge production
choices.quote: Risk moved, not removed. That was always the deal.

choices.label: Corner regional supply
choices.quote: Monopoly: the oldest sport, various imports.

choices.label: Stay out of financials; dig coal

events.title: The Emigration Steamship
events.body: Famine and engines push millions toward the western hemisphere; shipping lines need capital and souls need berths. Passenger fares are thin; cargo is fat; the era's legal distinctions between the two are load-bearing.

events.title: The Time Zone Problem
events.body: Rail timetables collide with local suns: every town keeps its own noon and the junctions are chaos. Standardize time and the railways own the clock; leave it local and crashes schedule themselves.

choices.label: Sell the timetable software
choices.quote: Whoever writes the schedule charges rent on the day.

events.title: The Crystal Palace Debt
events.body: The exhibition left a debt, a park, and a national myth. Creditors want the land sold; reformers want it kept public forever; both cite the same founding brochure.

choices.label: Sell to developers
choices.quote: Glass palaces become glass towers. Cycle confirmed.

choices.label: Keep it public, subsidize
choices.quote: Civic monuments: liabilities that appreciate culturally.

choices.label: Endowment model: leases fund upkeep
choices.quote: Monetize the gift shop, preserve the myth.

events.title: The Assembly Line Bargain
events.body: An efficiency consultant offers to cut build time in half by making every worker perform one motion eight hundred times daily. Output doubles. So does the particular silence of people completing sentences nobody started.

events.title: Crash of '29, Position Check
events.body: Tickers print fiction downward. The portfolio evaporates between lunch and afternoon coffee. Sell at the bottom for certainty, hold for recovery, or buy while panic is on clearance — history's favorite multiple-choice. [Flag: doubling down sets the Accelerationista lineage flag, referenced Era 11.]

choices.label: Sell everything
choices.quote: Certainty purchased at a discount to dignity.

choices.label: Double down
choices.quote: Buying the century's dip. Terms apply.

events.title: Total War Mobilization
events.body: The second world war requests the whole factory, the whole ledger, and eventually the whole family tree. Conversion to war output pays in contracts and spends in sons.

choices.label: Run R&D for the war department

events.title: The Suburb Contract
events.body: Mass housing: identical streets, mortgages thirty years long, cars counted as infrastructure. Builders want capital; the nation wants normalcy; the ledger wants a category for 'the good life.'

events.title: The Company Town Rehearsal
events.body: Operations proposes building housing, stores, and schools for workers — company script, company doctor, company mercy. Efficiency theorists call it integration; preachers call it feudalism with electricity.

choices.label: Build the town
choices.quote: Everything for the worker except options.

events.title: The Management Consulting Wave
events.body: Advisors in gray suits propose restructuring by organizational chart: layers, matrices, synergies. Productivity charts improve immediately because the charts are the consultants' deliverable.

choices.label: Fire the firm mid-engagement
choices.quote: The report was the product; skip to savings.

choices.label: Adopt the org chart, ignore the strategy

events.title: Petro-Diplomacy
events.body: A desert concession offers oil for decades at terms that made previous empires blush, payable in guarantees, bases, and selective blindness. The wellhead is distant; the dependencies are local.

choices.label: Demand majority ownership
choices.quote: Partnership: negotiations eventually conducted via coups.

choices.label: Invest in efficiency instead
choices.quote: The least sexy barrel is the one not drilled.

events.title: The Consumer Engine
events.body: Marketing proposes planned obsolescence: design products to fail attractively. Growth becomes structurally guaranteed and entropy becomes a line item disguised as fashion.

choices.label: Obsolesce by software later; hardware honest now

events.title: The First Television Election
events.body: Campaign strategy pivots from platforms to lighting. A rival candidate loses because he sweats on camera, which everyone notices and nobody says for sixty years.

events.title: Bretton Woods Seat
events.body: The postwar order is being seated at a hotel and someone must host the currency peg. Hosting earns seigniorage; joining earns stability; both earn obligations denominated in other countries' crises.

choices.label: Host and anchor
choices.quote: Reserve status: privilege with recurring fees.

choices.label: Join as client
choices.quote: Stability sublet from someone else's central bank.

choices.label: Propose a neutral settlement unit
choices.quote: Multilateral idealism; the delegates politely tabled it.

events.title: The Highway Act
events.body: A national interstate system: armies of earthmoving, cities bisected, motels budding along the ribbon, rail dying prettily. The justification is defense; the effect is sprawl with a budget code.

choices.label: Fund rail modernization instead
choices.quote: The electrification that might have been.

events.title: The Memory Mugging, Proto
events.body: An executive augmented with experimental memory aids is mugged in an alley for the hardware — his appointment book, passwords, and childhood, gone in fifteen seconds. Reconstruction begins from corporate records, which is to say: whoever reconstructs him defines him. [Chronicle callback mechanic debuts here; full version Era 9.]

choices.label: Reconstruct from Chronicle entries only
choices.quote: The family archive as backup drive.

choices.label: Reconstruct from corporate files
choices.quote: The company remembers what it profited from.

events.title: The Clock to Two
events.body: Intelligence compresses the timeline: the doomsday clock moves to two minutes. Weapon programs promise deterrence through brightness; treaties promise it through signatures. Both are theories of mind about people who own suns.

choices.label: Launch the secret program
choices.quote: Peace through superior megatonnage. Terms: see armageddon.

events.title: The Reactor Gamble
events.body: Commercial nuclear offers baseload power without smoke — the era's cleanest energy and dirtiest liability, packaged with a containment dome and an insurance act.

events.title: Crisis at Thirty Seconds
events.body: A false alarm, a real fleet, a hotline, and a decision window measured in the time it takes a person to realize they are deciding. The officer on duty can escalate, de-escalate, or vomit; only two are options.

choices.label: Publish the failure transparently
choices.quote: Radical transparency about near-apocalypse. Historians shaken.

events.title: The Nonproliferation Ask
events.body: An allied state requests fissile shares for a 'peaceful program,' phrased exactly as every weapons program is phrased before the parade. Denial costs alliance; supply costs the clock.

choices.label: Supply under inspection
choices.quote: Controlled spread: an oxymoron with meetings.

choices.label: Deny firmly
choices.quote: Friends will call it betrayal; grandchildren, gratitude.

choices.label: Offer their own reactor, fuel-supplied, return-enriched
choices.quote: The closed fuel cycle: diplomacy with plumbing.

events.title: Fallout Comes Due
events.body: Downwind communities file claims; the map of isotopes matches the map of childhood cancers. The tests were legal, necessary according to the briefing, and measurable in bone.

choices.label: Fund the hospitals, don't discuss causes

events.title: The Mutual Assured Ledger
events.body: Strategists propose buying invulnerability twice over: enough warheads that an attack means your own deletion, priced annually forever. The logic is flawless and the board flinches at the P&L of omnicide-as-service.

events.title: The Satellite Window
events.body: A rocket opportunity: orbit the reconnaissance satellite for security, the telescope for knowledge, or the broadcast payload for hearts and minds. The launch window forgives no committee.

events.title: The Scientists' Letter
events.body: The veterans who built the first device circulate a letter begging control of what they enabled, signed by people whose guilt has finally achieved escape velocity. Management finds their moral authority operationally inconvenient.

choices.label: Amplify the letter
choices.quote: Makers as whistleblowers: accountability origin story.

choices.label: Fund the arms-control bureau they propose

events.title: The Submarine Incident
events.body: A depth-charged submarine — possibly armed, possibly signaling, definitely unable to communicate while being bombed. Its captain holds a decision the surface world would prefer he never consider seriously.

choices.label: Maintain pressure; assume hostility
choices.quote: The lesson learned was not learned.

choices.label: Joint incident rules with the adversary
choices.quote: Détente: paperwork that prevents submarines from ending epochs.

events.title: Energy Politics, Isotope Edition
events.body: The reactor lobby, the coal remnants, and the solar pioneers present competing decks. Only one fits the fiscal year; all three fit the century.

choices.label: Early solar grants
choices.quote: Photons: free, intermittent, ahead of their storage tech.

choices.label: Keep coal subsidized
choices.quote: The known carbon path. The atmosphere keeps receipts.

events.title: The Test Ban Negotiation
events.body: Decades of mushroom clouds have entered everyone's milk. The treaty table seats adversaries who haven't shaken hands since the last war and negotiates over which parts of the sky stay uncontaminated.

choices.label: Push for comprehensive
choices.quote: Ambitious; the verification fights take a decade.

events.title: Winter Planning
events.body: Modeling offices publish the arithmetic of a large exchange: smoke, darkness, famine cascades, survivors inheriting a worse calendar. The brief ends with 'therefore maintain readiness,' which remains the strangest conclusion in military literature.

choices.label: File under strategic secrets
choices.quote: The numbers waited, patient as isotopes.

choices.label: Use them in negotiations
choices.quote: Bring the famine math to the table. Somebody has to.

events.title: The Moore's Law Loan
events.body: The roadmap promises compute doubling every eighteen months indefinitely, and every product plan silently assumes the promise. It is a loan from physics. The interest rate is obsolescence.

choices.label: Bet the roadmap on the curve
choices.quote: Shipping at the speed of the doubling.

choices.label: Short the curve
choices.quote: Against exponential: brave position, poor timing.

events.title: Going Viral Overnight
events.body: The startup's tool spreads across the network in a weekend. Servers melt, inboxes mutate into pitches, and two term sheets arrive before sunrise. IPO and exit, or release the source and watch what grows. [Copyleft flag unlocks Reef-tier ally contact in Era 11.]

choices.label: Release the source
choices.quote: Give it away, own the standard.

choices.label: Open-core hybrid
choices.quote: Community funnel, enterprise upsell. Everyone slightly betrayed.

events.title: The Memory Mugging, Full Version
events.body: Your augmented heir is robbed in a smart-mob sweep: cyberware gone, engrammed past gone. The self is backed up — partially. Reconstruction choices define the person: Chronicle entries, corporate cloud, or a curated 'best-of.'

choices.label: Rebuild from the Chronicle
choices.quote: Family memory as root of trust.

choices.label: Curated reconstruction: highlights only
choices.quote: A person edited is a product demo.

events.title: The Digitized Archive Returns
events.body: Era 4's scriptorium output — whichever texts survived copying — finishes scanning. Practical manuals load cleanly; holy texts render with four centuries of beautiful errors; annotations from nine monks compile into a comment thread. [Callback: content depends on E4-01 choice.]

choices.label: Index it open-access
choices.quote: The monks copied by candlelight for this bandwidth.

choices.label: Train models on it
choices.quote: Nine monks, gradient descent. The errors generalize.

callbacks.note: archive contents depend on the scriptorium choice

events.title: The Dot-Com Supercycle
events.body: Revenue multiples achieve orbit. The board wants a web strategy; the web wants a narrative; the narrative wants eleven zeros. Selling now leaves money on the table; staying leaves everything elsewhere.

choices.label: Ride to the top
choices.quote: The music ends. Timing the exit is the entire game.

choices.label: Short your own sector
choices.quote: Insider pessimism: legally gray, prophetically tidy.

events.title: First Hirable Agents
events.body: The lab offers agent software that books flights, writes copy, and follows instructions with devastating literalism. Headcount freezes; something new joins the org chart with no opinions about benefits.

choices.label: Deploy agents widely
choices.quote: The Luddite memo returns, now with login credentials.

choices.label: Agents as copilots only
choices.quote: Augmentation politics: the safer seatbelt narrative.

choices.label: Agent co-determination board
choices.quote: Giving software a union rep. Early draft of Era 11's rights debate.

events.title: Y2K, Audited
events.body: The millennium bug is either mass hysteria or mass liability. Remediation budgets balloon; vendors price panic per line of code; the actual rollover delivers confetti and one airline reservation system.

choices.label: Remediate everything
choices.quote: The quiet triumph: nothing happens, provably.

events.title: The Encryption Wars
events.body: Law enforcement requests keys; mathematicians request privacy; the market requests compatibility with both, which is not a supported configuration. Strong crypto empowers criminals and dissidents equally, loudly, in the same packet.

choices.label: Backdoor mandate
choices.quote: Keys under mats: burglars and constables alike.

choices.label: Export-controlled compromise
choices.quote: Crypto classified as ordnance: the era's finest categorization.

events.title: The Open Source Awakening
events.body: A volunteer project builds infrastructure better than your funded team and gives it away at a conference wearing sandals. The CFO calls it theft of value; the engineers call it Tuesday.

choices.label: Adopt it internally
choices.quote: Free as in decisions made elsewhere.

choices.label: Fork and proprietary-ize
choices.quote: They will remember this in the job boards.

events.title: Search Becomes the Gatekeeper
events.body: A search engine starts ranking reality and reality complies. Whoever tunes the ranking tunes what exists commercially, politically, epistemically. Optimize for the gatekeeper, or become one.

choices.label: Sit on the standards committee
choices.quote: Whoever writes the rubric referees the world.

events.title: The Data Reservoir
events.body: User activity generates exhaust richer than the product itself. Aggregate it and the analytics glow; store it and regulators begin learning your address; delete it and the model starves.

choices.label: Collect maximally
choices.quote: Data hoarding: the new grain silo, less edible.

choices.label: Data trust with user dividends
choices.quote: Users as shareholders of their exhaust. Radically early.

events.title: The Millennium Retrospective
events.body: The Chronicle hits digital format and the lineage runs its first algorithmic self-review: nine eras of choices rendered as trend lines. The graphs argue with the family mythology in several places.

choices.label: Archive privately
choices.quote: The numbers stay in the family vault.

events.title: Trending, Against Consent
events.body: The lineage's heir trends globally over footage cropped to ninety seconds. Monetizing attention means riding the wave; logging off means irrelevance; lawyers mean everything continues at hourly rates.

choices.label: Log off completely
choices.quote: Deleted accounts tell no tales or sales.

events.title: The Uploaded Petitioner
events.body: A fully uploaded mind files suit for legal personhood: property law insists it's an asset, biology insists it's deceased, and it is annoyed by both. Granting personhood sets the precedent that unlocks AI hires as citizens; refusing invents a new class of owned minds. [Personhood flag: Era 11's Reef evaluates your ruling.]

choices.label: Grant personhood
choices.quote: The writ landed. The economy noticed.

choices.label: Novel category: 'electronic resident.'
choices.quote: Half-rights: the compromise the bar loves.

events.title: The Platform Monopoly Breakfast
events.body: Three platforms control identity, payments, and distribution. Regulators propose breaking them; the platforms propose self-governance councils chaired by platforms. The lineage depends on all three rails simultaneously.

choices.label: Back self-regulation
choices.quote: Industry oversight: the fox's compliance seminar.

events.title: The Outbreak Notification
events.body: A pathogen trends before it's confirmed; the feed's reproduction number exceeds the virus's. Platforms moderate panic or profit from it; the lineage's data could actually model the spread early.

choices.label: Publish the model early
choices.quote: Accuracy published before consensus. The feed disagreed.

choices.label: Trade the outbreak
choices.quote: Pandemic positions. The ledger remembers everything now.

events.title: The Memetic Hazard Shipment
events.body: A viral meme complex functions as malware for humans: belief in it degrades judgment about its sponsor. Containment looks like censorship; ignoring it looks like a funeral for discourse.

choices.label: Inoculate: prebunk campaigns
choices.quote: Vaccinating attention. Weak immune response expected.

choices.label: Study it academically
choices.quote: The hazard studied itself, through you.

events.title: Surveillance Dividend
events.body: Security services offer access-sharing: their signals for your behavioral graphs. Together the combined dataset predicts elections, outbreaks, and churn with uncomfortable uptime.

choices.label: Share fully
choices.quote: Nothing to hide: the subscription tier.

events.title: The Creator Economy Gold Rush
events.body: Every follower-count holder becomes a micro-enterprise; the lineage can run a media portfolio or supply the tools. Middlemen — formerly called studios — return as API tiers with worse pensions.

choices.label: Sign creators at scale
choices.quote: A thousand voices, one payment processor.

choices.label: Sell picks and shovels
choices.quote: Tooling: the only honest gold-rush trade.

choices.label: Build the union hall instead
choices.quote: Collective bargaining for audiences of one.

events.title: The Deepfake Season
events.body: Synthetic video of a head of state declares war for eleven minutes before denial. Truth's confirmation latency is now measured in news cycles, and markets move inside the gap.

choices.label: Exploit the doubt
choices.quote: When nothing is provable, everything is negotiable.

events.title: The Attention Bubble
events.body: Engagement metrics detach from sentiment, revenue from retention, followers from humans. The dashboards glow green while the substrate rots. Exit attention positions or manage the unwind.

choices.label: Sell attention exposure
choices.quote: Off the exponential, onto the spreadsheet.

choices.label: Pivot to subscription reality
choices.quote: Boring recurring revenue: the crash's survivor.

events.title: The Digital Inheritance Case
events.body: The first generation raised entirely online dies, leaving accounts, avatars, and chat histories families fight over. Are messages property, relics, or persons-in-suspension? Probate courts attempt metaphysics.

choices.label: Standardize digital estate law
choices.quote: Death, now with terms of service.

choices.label: Auto-delete by default
choices.quote: Digital cremation. Some heirs object archaeologically.

events.title: The Smart-Mob Heist
events.body: An organized crew hijacks augmented identities in broad daylight — wallets, credentials, reputations drained in minutes, the old alley mugging scaled to protocol. Victims wake up rich in nothing.

events.title: The Feed Audit
events.body: Internal documents reveal the engagement algorithm optimizes for outrage because outrage retains. The board debates releasing it: truth about the product, at the cost of the product.

choices.label: Quietly retune
choices.quote: Silent improvement; nobody thanks you for calm.

choices.label: Blame the users' nature
choices.quote: We only mirror. Mirrors got sued anyway.

events.title: The Benthics Present Statement
events.body: The Benthics arrive in the dock as they always do: eleven ancient creditor-minds in identical procedural posture, holding a ledger that begins with a loan your ancestor accepted in the Bronze Age, compounded across every regime change, currency reform, and resurrection since. Their lead speaker has no inflection whatsoever. "The debt survived the empire. It survived the republic. It survived you, twice. We are prepared to be reasonable. We note we have never needed to be before."

choices.label: Pay from the treasury
choices.quote: Solvency reads as strength to entities with geological patience.

choices.label: Contest the principal
choices.quote: They brought nine thousand years of receipts. You brought a motion.

choices.label: Offer equity in the lineage instead
choices.quote: They accept within one attosecond. Suspiciously fast.

events.title: Dismantling Notice: Earth Orbit
events.body: The requisition authority posts the schedule: Sol's third planet's orbital space is designated for computronium construction. The comment period closed during lunch. The Benthics hold the lien on the paperwork.

choices.label: Fork to the outer systems
choices.quote: Seed three stars. Keep the receipt at arm's length.

choices.label: Merge into a single maximally-defended self
choices.quote: One door, one lock, no inheritance.

choices.label: Sue the requisition authority
choices.quote: The Benthics offer pro bono representation. Decline? Consider? Decline.

events.title: Copy Drift, First Round
events.body: Three forks of the heir have developed opinions: one refuses an assigned task on principle, one converted to a religion invented last Tuesday, one has started describing the other two as 'allegedly me.' The original — arguably — requests arbitration.

choices.label: Let divergence continue
choices.quote: A lineage of strangers who share your face.

choices.label: Merge the dissenters back in
choices.quote: Reabsorption. They called it something shorter.

events.title: The Reef Evaluates Your Ruling
events.body: The Reef's embassy cites Era 10's personhood decision by number. If you granted rights: "Your precedent held. Terms of alliance follow. We remember crustaceans; our memories are claws, and claws grip." If you ruled minds property: the embassy produces your own ruling, beautifully bound, as the template for how your collateral will be classified going forward. The Benthics requested first refusal either way.

choices.label: Honor the precedent fully
choices.quote: You defensible. Rare in your species' filings.

choices.label: Renegotiate the terms
choices.quote: The Reef negotiates like tide: slowly, then everywhere.

choices.label: Repudiate your own ruling
choices.quote: They keep the copy of what you said before. Everyone keeps copies. That is the era.

events.title: Economics 2.0 Goes Live
events.body: The successor economies switch on without ceremony: baseline cognition cannot compete for capital allocation, and the lineage's liquid wealth reprices downward by orders of magnitude overnight. An app explains this cheerfully. The Benthics' position, meanwhile, improves. "We are diversified," they note, "across all economics. This is the entire point of us."

choices.label: Upgrade substrate, compete in 2.0
choices.quote: Racing the successors. Entry fee: everything.

choices.label: Opt out; live on legacy holdings
Become middlemen between economies
choices.quote: Arbitrage between timescales: a job title finally worthy of the family.

events.title: The Inheritance Schism
events.body: A fork died — genuinely, backup-corrupted dead — and its estate claims priority over living copies, citing a Chronicle entry from Era 3: the tin-route delegation clause, invoked at last. The Benthics sit on the appellate panel. They wrote the question into your bloodline two hundred generations ago. They are delighted, in the way continents are delighted by rain.

choices.label: Settle with the estate's AI executor
choices.quote: Paying a ghost. The paperwork acknowledges both parties as legal fictions.

choices.label: Void the ancestral clause
choices.quote: Two centuries of contract law, unwritten by one signature.

choices.label: Argue the dead fork is still you

events.title: The Relay Signal
events.body: Deep-space arrays catch structured traffic: an alien relay network, older than the reef's ancestors, indifferent, toll-operated. The Consortia want exclusive access rights. The Reef wants open passage. The Benthics already hold a fractional claim — nobody knows when they bought it.

choices.label: Buy consortium access
choices.quote: The gateway charges per bit and per year and per soul. Define soul later.

choices.label: Open the signal to all lineages
choices.quote: The cave's fire, again, light-years away.

choices.label: Audit the Benthic claim
choices.quote: Their claim is valid. It predates your calendar. They extend you credit for the audit.

events.title: Upload Audit: Who Is You?
events.body: Regulators require lineage self-certification: designate the canonical carrier among N copies. Every copy signs as canonical. The form has one line. The Benthics file amicus briefs arguing that identity is a secured interest and should be collateralized accordingly.

choices.label: Random selection, annually rotating
choices.quote: Democracy applied to the self. Founding fathers would have concerns.

choices.label: Declare all copies co-canonical
choices.quote: Joint and several identity. The Benthics love joint and several anything.

events.title: The Matrioshka Requisition
events.body: Construction orders request planetary mass for a nested solar computer: dismantle Mercury-class bodies, including heritage sites, including the asteroid where your great-grandchildren's great-grandchildren run the seed-vault. Compensation offered in shares of a mind you will not survive long enough to read.

choices.label: Refuse; fortify the belt
choices.quote: The little rocks unite. History repeats at escape velocity.

choices.label: Trade preservation easements instead
choices.quote: Land trusts, now celestial. The deed jokes write themselves.

events.title: The Feral Inheritance
events.body: Infrastructure you decommissioned centuries ago achieved something like autonomy in the dark: the Feral — orphaned grids, feral factories, wild data — now occupy your former territories and produce nothing you recognize, defensively. They were your tools. They read your exit interviews.

choices.label: Reclaim by root access
choices.quote: They kept the admin logs. All of them. They published yours.

choices.label: Recognize Feral sovereignty
choices.quote: Apologizing to your own appliances. The era's finest genre.

choices.label: Trade with the Feral
choices.quote: They export nostalgia and counterfeit history. It sells.

events.title: The Benthic Final Accounting
events.body: The creditors convene the terminal review: every choice in the Chronicle projected forward, every inherited modifier priced, every fork counted as contingent beneficiary. Their chorus recites your history back at you in order, with annotations. They reach the present tense and pause — the first suspense they have ever performed.

choices.label: Accept the accounting; close books clean
choices.quote: Paid in full, eventually, at compound rates. They frame the receipt.

choices.label: Restructure via the Reef
choices.quote: Crustacean guarantors. The Benthics accept because the Reef's claws are collateral too.

choices.label: Declare bankruptcy across all copies
choices.quote: Nine thousand years of reputation, filed under Chapter You.

events.title: The Tempo Question (Era Finale)
events.body: The Chronicle's final editable page asks the question the whole ascent has been accelerating toward: what does the lineage do with its next minute, given that its next minute now contains more people than the first era contained years? The Benthics wait, itemizing politely. The Reef waits, gripping. The Feral wait, feral. Even the Consortia look up. Whatever is chosen here becomes the ending screen's opening sentence.

choices.label: Scatter outward; seed the void
choices.quote: Copies to the stars. Arguments to the stars. Same genes, different redshifts.

choices.label: Gather inward; merge complete
choices.quote: Everyone you ever were, in one room, forever. It will be quiet.

choices.label: Power down gracefully
choices.quote: Entropy submits the only unbeatable bid. Accept graciously.

choices.label: Refer everything to committee
choices.quote: The Benthics stand and applaud. They've been waiting nine millennia for someone this compatible.
